name: the solar system
plain: The Sun and the eight planets on circles at their semi-major axes, each at its mean longitude today (JPL's approximate elements, Standish; within 24 degrees for Mercury, 11 for Mars, 6 for the rest), and Pluto on its tilted orbit drawn as a circle. Bodies are at their true radii but never under 3 to 7 pixels, so their sizes are exaggerated at almost every zoom; their night sides are drawn at three tenths of full light, not black; a ring marks the Earth. The Kuiper belt's points (30 to 50 au) are an illustration.

carrier.state: the Sun and the eight planets on circles at their semi-major axes, each at its mean longitude for the host's clock

basis.note: 'How the rungs meet': each scene moves its own origin and frame with z, so that at the shared edge the two draw the same thing in the same place

parts.what: the Kuiper belt's points, 30 to 50 au

source.external: E. M. Standish, 'Keplerian Elements for Approximate Positions of the Major Planets', JPL Solar System Dynamics

views.reads: the rung's marks at the zoom's metres per pixel

budget.quantity: what drawing a tile coarse may move against drawing it fine: the draw allocator's tolerance (Acuity, eps_px). It is not a bound on the picture's faithfulness to the holon.
